candidates.title: Fixing prompt schedule drift
candidates.summary: Barry rebuilt the prompt scheduling system to calculate the week purely from time, preventing schedule drift and back-filled existing users with a migration.
candidates.heading: ✍️ Brief > Problems I solved along the way
candidates.quote: I rebuilt it so the week is calculated purely from time (from sign-up to now), so the schedule can no longer drift, and I back-filled existing users with a one-off migration.

candidates.title: Fixed silent alert failures
candidates.summary: Barry identified WhatsApp's 24-hour session rule caused silent alert failures and added an automatic fallback to a pre-approved template message with tests for both paths.
candidates.heading: 🌸 In My Time > Problems I solved along the way
candidates.quote: Admin alerts weren't arriving, yet the messaging API reported every send as successful. The root cause was WhatsApp's 24-hour session rule: free-form messages are only delivered while a conversation is open. I added an automatic fallback to a pre-approved template

candidates.title: Fixing data quality issues

candidates.title: Improving Answer Evaluator Accuracy
candidates.summary: Barry improved the answer evaluator by requesting evidence from the judge, testing the evaluator with unit tests, and refining prompts to reduce false positives.
candidates.heading: Ask Barry > Answer-quality evaluation (Stage 6) > Results (27 Sep 2026)
candidates.quote: Ask the judge for evidence, not a verdict. The judge lists each claim with a quoted supporting passage... Test the evaluator too. Early versions failed correct answers because of formatting... Each fix came with a unit test.

candidates.title: Handled credential exposure incident
candidates.summary: Barry rotated all exposed API secrets, rebuilt Git history as a single clean commit, and locked the repository with a strict .gitignore after a secret scanner flagged credentials in an early commit.
candidates.heading: ✍️ Brief > Problems I solved along the way
candidates.quote: an automated secret scanner flagged API credentials in an early commit. I rotated every exposed secret (Google, Microsoft and Twilio) so the leaked values were dead, rebuilt the Git history as a single clean commit, and locked the repository down

candidates.title: Privacy by design in server architecture
candidates.summary: Barry designed a server that relays answers without storing message text or transcriptions, keeping only minimal metadata and avoiding personal data collection.
candidates.heading: 🌸 In My Time > Privacy by design: the "shallow room"
candidates.quote: The server relays each answer in the same request and stores nothing. It keeps no message text and no transcriptions, and media is forwarded by reference and never downloaded.

candidates.title: Designing for end-of-life privacy
candidates.summary: Barry designed a system that never assumes user death, pausing and sending a check-in only to the custodian, with closing steps starting after family confirmation.
candidates.heading: 🌸 In My Time > Privacy by design: the "shallow room" > Designing for the end of life
candidates.quote: The system never assumes a death. If an author goes quiet, it pauses patiently, then sends one gently worded check-in to the custodian, never to the author.

candidates.title: Implementing Least Privilege Access
candidates.summary: Barry configured identities and roles in code to enforce least privilege, disabled API keys, and used Microsoft Entra ID for authentication, ensuring the app refused to start without a secret key in production.
candidates.heading: Ask Barry > Security
candidates.quote: Least privilege, as code: the identities and roles live in `infra/identity.tf`, and tests fail if any identity gets a broad role such as Owner or Contributor.

candidates.title: Implemented keyless security
candidates.summary: Barry implemented keyless security from the first commit, using managed identities and least-privilege roles defined in Terraform, with tests to prevent key usage.
candidates.heading: Housing Pipeline Ireland > Security
candidates.quote: Keyless from the first commit. No API keys or passwords anywhere... Key-based access is switched off on every Azure resource, roles are least-privilege and defined in Terraform, and a test (`tests/test_no_keys.py`) fails if any module reads a key-style setting.

candidates.title: Azure sign-in with Entra ID
candidates.summary: Barry configured Azure to sign in using Entra ID instead of keys, created identities and roles, tested token acceptance, and set up secrets to avoid storing keys in Terraform or GitHub.
candidates.heading: Stage 3: Azure setup > Step 8: Sign in with Entra ID instead of keys (ASK-8)
candidates.quote: The nightly index refresh signs in with GitHub OIDC (ASK-34), so GitHub stores no Azure secret at all. Terraform creates the ask-barry-github app registration with a federated credential that Entra accepts only from this repo's main branch.
